insights.headline: Record central-bank gold buying meets 15-year-high real yields as India heads into the festive season
insights.summary: Gold opened October firmer as softer US inflation data cooled bets on another Fed hike this month, while record 288.9 tonnes of central-bank buying in Q2 floored prices against near-record real yields. On MCX, gold futures held near ₹1.49–1.50 lakh per 10 grams and silver around ₹2.25 lakh per kg, with the rupee’s slide to a two-month low keeping domestic prices elevated. Festive and wedding buying — lighter jewellery, EMI schemes and old-gold exchanges — is expected to support physical demand into Dhanteras and Diwali, while IBJA’s chief sees gold eyeing $4,100 after breaking $4,250 support.
points: Central banks bought a record 288.9t of gold in Q2 2026 (+62% yoy), buying into the dip; China added for a 21st straight month.
Softer US inflation dimmed October Fed-hike bets; gold reopened at $4,182 while 10-year TIPS yields sit near a record.
MCX gold held ₹1.49–1.50 lakh/10g and silver near ₹2.25 lakh/kg as the rupee fell to a two-month low on the global bond rout.
New Indian gold ETF folios fell from 12 lakh in January to ~4,000 a month as small savers moved to UPI-based digital gold.
Four SGB tranches are eligible for premature redemption in October; festive buyers favour lightweight jewellery and old-gold exchanges.

trending.title: Record central-bank buying sets gold’s floor
trending.summary: Official buyers absorbed a record 288.9t in Q2 while prices fell, China stacked for a 21st month, and the Bank of Korea is buying gold for the first time since 2013.

trending.title: October Fed-hike bets cool on soft inflation
trending.summary: Softer PCE data revived hopes the Fed holds in October, lifting gold off its September lows — though 5.34% 10-year yields keep the rebound capped.

trending.title: Rupee weakness keeps Indian prices elevated
trending.summary: The rupee hit a two-month low as the global bond rout deepened, cushioning domestic gold near ₹1.50 lakh even as dollar prices slipped.

trending.title: Festive buying adapts to record prices
trending.summary: With Dhanteras and Diwali near, buyers are choosing lighter pieces, EMI schemes and old-gold exchanges, while ETF investors wait out the correction.

trending.title: Silver waits for its turn
trending.summary: Silver fell three times as far as gold in September, then led the October bounce; analysts see a falling gold-to-silver ratio as the signal the sell-off is over.

items.title: Record 288.9t of central-bank gold buying in Q2 meets the highest real yields in 15 years
items.summary: Central banks bought a net 288.9 tonnes of gold in Q2 2026, up 62% year on year and the strongest second quarter on record. China added 20 tonnes, its 21st straight month of buying. Spot gold reopened October at $4,182, up 0.6%, but near-record real yields cap the rebound toward a $4,450 target. Silver, down 13.5% in September, led the bounce.

items.title: Gold inches higher as softer US inflation dims October Fed hike bets
items.summary: Gold edged up 0.5% to $4,175 an ounce after softer US inflation data cut October Fed rate-hike odds to 38% from 45%, with December still priced at 97%. TD Securities' Bart Melek told Reuters the worst of the correction may be over, while Tastylive's Ilya Spivak said incoming data will shape hike expectations. Markets now await Friday's jobs report; the dollar near a two-month high capped gains.

items.title: Gold rises ₹607 as rate-hold expectations strengthen; silver jumps ₹2,828
items.summary: MCX gold futures rose ₹607 to about ₹1,49,434 per 10 grams while silver’s December contract jumped ₹2,828 to about ₹2,25,680 per kg, Business Standard reports. Lower-than-expected US inflation data strengthened expectations that the Fed will hold rates, with Comex gold trading near $4,200 an ounce.

items.title: Gold futures rise to ₹1.50 lakh/10 gm on firm spot demand
items.summary: Gold for October delivery on the MCX rose ₹1,475, or 0.99%, to ₹1,50,511 per 10 grams as speculators built fresh positions on firm spot demand, PTI reports. Gold futures in New York gained 0.59% to $4,182.06 an ounce.

items.title: Gold, silver prices edge higher: How festive demand could shape the outlook
items.summary: Domestic gold and silver futures edged higher ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali, CNBC-TV18 reports, quoting analysts on how festive demand could shape the near-term price outlook.

items.title: New gold ETF folios collapse from 12 lakh in January to ~4,000 as first-time buyers drift to digital gold
items.summary: Investors opened 12 lakh new gold ETF folios in January at the cycle peak; by late summer net new folios ran at roughly 4,000 a month. August inflows still rose 67% to ₹2,597 crore, but from existing investors — institutions hold most ETF assets. Digital gold via UPI apps averaged ₹2,500 crore a month from June to August, up 110% year on year.

items.title: Rupee drops to two-month low as global bond rout deepens, oil jumps
items.summary: The rupee fell 0.5% to 96.3150 per dollar, its weakest in two months and sharpest single-day drop in over two months, the Economic Times reports. Surging global bond yields and Brent crude reclaiming $100 — after China suspended oil product exports — pressured the currency; dollar sales by state-run banks limited the fall.

items.title: Silver (XAG) Forecast: PCE Rally Fails as $60.84 Retracement Comes Under Pressure
items.summary: FXEmpire says silver failed to hold its post-PCE rally and fell back to the $60.84 half-retracement of its all-time high, with Tuesday's $60.30 low as the line buyers must defend. The analyst notes a strong ADP jobs print keeps Fed-hawk arguments alive into Friday's payrolls report: a weak number could lift silver back through $61.04, a firm one leaves $60.30 exposed.

items.title: Gold price future roadmap: 6% September fall meets Diwali demand hopes
items.summary: Gold fell about 6.5% in September, its worst month since June, after Fed tightening and a 10-year US yield at 5.293% — highest since 2007, Mint reports. Brickwork Ratings' Rajeev Sharan expects firm but range-bound prices through Dussehra, Dhanteras, Diwali and winter wedding demand; Monarch PMS' Dhruv Joglekar points to festive physical buying plus central-bank accumulation.

items.title: How Trump's Gold Tariffs Created a $100 NY-London Basis Gap
items.summary: A deep dive into how US gold tariff moves opened a $100-an-ounce premium of New York futures over London spot: CBP's 39% bar reclassification in July 2025, a 0% order that September, and the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling that replaced tariffs with 10%/15% rates, plus the WGC's January 2026 IEEPA investment-gold exemption.

items.title: SGB premature redemption October 2026: 4 tranches eligible for early exit
items.summary: RBI scheduled premature redemption for four SGB tranches — 2019-20 Series V and VI and 2020-21 Series I and VII, Livemint reports. Deadlines: Oct 5 (Series V, redeems Oct 15), Oct 9 (Series VII, Oct 19), Oct 19 (Series I, Oct 28), Oct 21 (Series VI, Oct 30). Value uses IBJA's 3-day 999-gold average. From FY27 the capital-gains exemption applies only if held to maturity, so early exit may be taxed.

items.title: BOK to add gold to its coffers for the first time since 2013
items.summary: The Bank of Korea will buy about one metric ton of domestically produced gold in December — its first physical purchase since February 2013, Aju Press reports. A settlement system completes December 14; the gold will be bought in won via KRX/KSD from domestic output. The BOK held 104.4 tonnes at end-August and resumed gold exposure via a $250 million gold ETF position in Q2.

items.title: Gold’s 15% correction from its ₹1.76 lakh peak splits experts on whether the dip is a buying opportunity
items.summary: Gold corrected about 15% from its January peak of ₹1,76,305 per 10 grams to ₹1,51,301 in mid-September, after a 197% rally since August 2023. Nippon India MF’s Vikram Dhawan warns elevated yields and possible further Fed tightening keep volatility high. WGC data puts H1 2026 Indian ETF demand up 163% at 23.5 tonnes, while jewellery buyers choose lighter pieces and old-gold exchanges.

items.title: IBJA chief Kothari: gold broke $4,250 support, eyes $4,100; silver's $62.5 neckline gives way
items.summary: IBJA president Prithviraj Kothari says gold and silver slid further ahead of the US jobs report, with monthly losses of 8.5% and 13.5%. Softer August PCE cut October-hike odds to 38%, though a December hike is priced at 87%. Technically both metals look weak: gold broke $4,250 support with $4,100 and $4,000 next; silver cracked its $62.5 neckline, with $60 and $57 next.

items.title: Gold price at $4,158/oz after ISM Manufacturing PMI dips to 54.5, prices shoot higher
items.summary: September's ISM Manufacturing PMI eased to 54.5, but the prices index jumped to 77.9% from 71.1%, flagging cost pressure. Spot gold held near $4,158 an ounce. GivTrade's Waleed Said said October Fed-hike odds dropped below 50% after NY Fed chief Williams signaled no urgency for another hike and PCE printed a softer 3.4% — while the US 10-year yield stayed near 5.26%, its highest since 2007.

items.title: Unscrupulous jewellers may use fake stamps to mark your gold: GJC flags fraud risk as hallmarking charges rise
items.summary: Jewellery hallmarking charges rose 67% from Rs 45 to Rs 75 per article, and the Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council has warned the hike could push unscrupulous jewellers — especially in smaller cities — toward fake hallmark stamps, the Times of India reports. GJC has raised the concern with the consumer affairs minister and BIS.

items.title: Gold price will break $5,000/oz in H2 2027, and silver's run to $120 was driven by more than hype – Morgan Stanley's Gower
items.summary: Morgan Stanley's Amy Gower expects gold to trade back above $5,000/oz within a year, citing strong central-bank and ETF demand — she notes China's gold imports are on track for their highest since 2017. She sees support above $4,000/oz as fiscal-sustainability worries underpin prices, and says silver's run to $120 was driven by more than hype.
